correctness.rationale: In the finite classical S5 scope, reflexivity makes E^r test containment of the entire radius-r graph ball. The least r for all events is the maximum component diameter: deleting the far endpoint of a diametral pair supplies a counterexample at one step less, and zero diameter is already depth zero. An n−1 geodesic uses every vertex and an extra edge would shorten it. On that path, each agent's nonsingleton classes are a matching (a class of size ≥3 creates a triangle). Assigning every edge its nonempty set of agents with disjoint adjacent sets is therefore a bijection. Fixing one orientation per undirected labelled path counts the words without identifying distinct agent assignments; orientation reversal is already accounted for in n!/2. Grouping the next subset by size gives the stated recurrence, including the two-world value 2^k−1 and the separate one-world case. Independently iterated E on all events of all ordered frames for n=2..4, k=2,3 and reproduced the quoted counts through inclusion–exclusion over missing edge positions (python /workspace/branches/independent_math_checks.py, section 2). Separate direct enumeration of 239,549 small frames matched the path/subset count (python /workspace/branches/c8a972c1-f76e-41b1-9e78-60b522639569/independent_check.py). These are bounded reproductions, not a substitute for the general argument; the uploaded checker was inspected, not run.
